μενοῦνγε.der: from G3203 and G3767 (οὖν) and G1065 (γέ);
μενοῦνγε.as:
μεν-οῦν-γε = μὲν οὖν γε
nay rather: Ro 9:2010:18, Phl 3:8.†

μωρία.as:
** μωρία, -ας, ἡ
(< μωρός), [in LXX: Si 20:31*;]
foolishness: I Co 1:18, 21, 232:143:19.†

μετασχηματίζω.g: I change the outward appearance, transfigure, adapt
μετασχηματίζω.long: I change the outward appearance (the dress, the form of presentment) of something, transfigure; I adapt.
μετασχηματίζω.sd: to transfigure or disguise; figuratively, to apply (by accommodation)
μετασχηματίζω.der: from G3326 (μετά) and a derivative of G4976 (σχῆμα);
μετασχηματίζω.as:
** μετα-σχηματίζω,
[in LXX: IV Mac 9:22*;]
to change in fashion or appearance: c. acc. rei, τ. σῶμα, Phl 3:21; mid., seq. εἰς, II Co 11:13, 14; seq. ὡς, II Co 11:15; of a rhetorical device, to transfer by a fiction (Field, Notes, in l.), seq. εἰς, I Co 4:6.†
SYN.: μεταμορφόω, q.v.

μιμητής.as:
* μιμητής, -οῦ, ὁ
(< μιμέομαι),
in NT always (like the verb) in good sense, an imitator: I Co 4:1611:1, Eph 5:1, I Th 1:62:14, He 6:12.†

μέθυσος.as:
μέθυσος, -α, -ον
(also -ος, -ον; prop., only of women, but in late writers also = μεθυστικός, of men), [in LXX: Pr 23:21 (סבא) 26:9 (שִׁכּוֹר), Si 19:126:8, IV Mac 2:7*;]
drunken: I Co 5:116:10.†

μήτιγε.sd: not at all then, i.e. not to say (the rather still)
μήτιγε.as:
μή-τι-γε
(μήτι γε, Rec., L; μή τι γε, Tr.), >strengthened form of μήτι,
let alone: i.e. according to context;
(a)much less;
(b)much more: I Co 6:3.†

μολύνω.long: I soil, stain, pollute, defile, lit. and met.
μολύνω.as:
μολύνω,
[in LXX: Ge 37:31 (טבל), Is 59:3 (גּאל ni.), Za 14:2 (שׁכב ni.), Si 21:28, al.;]
to stain, soil, defile; in NT always symb. and fig.: I Co 8:7, Re 3:414:4.†
SYN.: μιαίνω, q.v.

μετέχω.long: I have a share of, participate in, share, partake of, am a member of.
μετέχω.sd: to share or participate; by implication, belong to, eat (or drink)
μετέχω.kj: be partaker, pertain, take part, use
μετέχω.as:
μετ-έχω,
[in LXX: Pr 5:17 (אֵת), 1:18, I Es 5:408:70, Si 51:28, al.;]
to partake of, share in: ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι τοῦ μετέχειν, I Co 9:10; c. gen. rei, I Co 9:1210:21, 30, He 2:14; in sacramental sense, ἑκ τ. ἐνὸς ἄρτου μ., I Co 10:17 (cf. MM, xvi); metaph., γάλακτος, He 5:13; of belonging to a tribe, He 7:13.†

μάκελλον.sd: a butcher's stall, meat market or provision-shop
μάκελλον.as:
*† μάκελλον, -ου, τό (Lat. macellum),
a meat-market: I Co 10:25 (v. Deiss., LAE, 274; MM, xvi).†

μαράνα.g: our Lord (Aramaic, in μαράνα θά, Our Lord, come!)

μωμάομαι.long: I blame, find fault with, slander.
μωμάομαι.as:
μωμάομαι, -ῶμαι
(< μῶμος), poët. and late prose, [in LXX: Pr 9:7 (מוּם), Wi 10:14, Si 31 (34):18*;]
to find fault with, blame: II Co 8:20; pass., II Co 6:3.†

μετοχή.as:
μετοχή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< μετέχω), [in LXX: Ps 121 (122):3א R (חבר pu.)*;]
sharing, fellowship: II Co 6:14.†

μολυσμός.as:
† μολυσμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< μολύνω), [in LXX: Je 23:15 (חֲנֻפָה), I Es 8:83, II Mac 5:27*;]
defilement: c. gen. obj., II Co 7:1 (Plut., FlJ).†

μάχη.long: (earlier: a battle, conflict, hence) in the sphere of words, etc: strife, contention, quarrel.
μάχη.as:
μάχη, -ης, ἡ
(< μάχομαι), [in LXX chiefly for רִיב;]
1.a fight.
2.a strife, contention, quarrel: II Co 7:5, II Ti 2:23, Ja 4:1; pl., Tit 3:9.†

μόχθος.as:
μόχθος, -ου, ὁ
(= Hom. μόγος), in cl. chiefly poët., [in LXX for תְּלָאָה, עָמָל, etc.;]
toil, labour, hardship, distress: II Co 11:27, I Th 2:9, II Th 3:8.†
SYN.: κόπος (q.v.), πόνος.

μεσίτης.long: (a) a mediator, intermediary, (b) a go-between, arbiter, agent of something good.
μεσίτης.sd: a go-between, i.e. (simply) an internunciator, or (by implication) a reconciler (intercessor)
μεσίτης.as:
† μεσίτης, -ου, ὁ
(< μέσος), [in LXX: Jb 9:33 (בַּיִן)*;]
an arbitrator, mediator: Ga 3:19; c. dupl. gen. pers., θεοῦ κ. ἀνθρώπων, I Ti 2:5; c. gen. rei, διαθήκης, He 8:69:1512:24; ὁ δε μ. ἑνὸς οὐκ ἔστιν, Ga 3:20 (v. Lft., in l.; and for exx. of this word in π., v. MM, xvi).†

μορφόω.as:
**† μορφόω, -ῶ
(< μορφή), [in Aq.: Is 44:13*;]
to form: fig., Ga 4:19 (cf. μετα-, συμ-μορφόω).†

μυκτηρίζω.long: (properly: I turn up the nose as a sign of contempt), I sneer at, disdain.
μυκτηρίζω.sd: to make mouths at, i.e. ridicule
μυκτηρίζω.der: from a derivative of the base of G3455 (μυκάομαι) (meaning snout, as that whence lowing proceeds);
μυκτηρίζω.as:
μυκτηρίζω
(< μυκτήρ, the nose), [in LXX: IV Ki 19:21, Jb 22:19, Ps 79 (80):6, al. (לעג), Pr 1:30 (נאץ) Pr 15:20 (בּזה), I Mac 7:34, al.;]
to turn up the nose or sneer at, mock: pass., Ga 6:7 (cf. ἐκ-μυκτηρίζω).†

μέγεθος.as:
μέγεθος, -ους, τό
(< μέγας), [in LXX chiefly for קוֹמָה;]
greatness: Eph 1:19 (cf. MM, xvi, s.v. μέγας).†

μεσότοιχον.long: a middle wall, partition wall, barrier.
μεσότοιχον.as:
*† μεσότοιχον, -ου, τό
(< μέσος, τοῖχος),
a partition wall: Eph 2:14 (not elsewhere, but v. LS, s.v. μεσότοιχος).†

μῆκος.as:
μῆκος, -εος (-ους), τό,
[in LXX chiefly for אֹרֶךְ;]
length: Eph 3:18, Re 21:16.†

μεθοδεία.long: (a way of search after something, an inquiry; a method), scheming, craftiness, deceit.
μεθοδεία.der: from a compound of G3326 (μετά) and G3593 (ὁδεύω) (compare "method");
μεθοδεία.as:
*† μεθ-οδία (Rec. -εία; cf. Bl., § 3, 5), -ας, ἡ
(< † μεθοδεύω, 1. to treat by rule. 2. to employ craft: IV Ki 19:27*)
craft, deceit: Eph 4:146:11 (not found elsewhere; v. AR, in l.).†

μωρολογία.der: from a compound of G3474 (μωρός) and G3004 (λέγω);

μακροχρόνιος.as:
μακρο-χρόνιος, -ον
(μακρός, χρόνος), [in LXX. μ. γίγνεσθαι, εἶναι (יָמִיםהַאֲרִיךְ), Ex 20:12, De 4:405:1617:20*;]
of long duration, longlived: Eph 6:3(LXX).†

μεγάλως.as:
μεγάλως,
adv.,
[in LXX for גָּדוֹל, etc.;]
greatly: Phl 4:10.†

μυέομαι.long: I initiate, instruct; pass: I am disciplined, learn (a lesson).
μυέομαι.sd: to initiate, i.e. (by implication) to teach
μυέομαι.as:
** μυέω, -ῶ
(< μύω, to shut the mouth), [in LXX: III Mac 2:30*;]
to initiate into the mysteries (so chiefly in cl.; LXX, III Mac 2:30); hence, to instruct: pass., Phl 4:12 (RV, I have learned the secret).†

μετακινέω.long: trans: I move away, dislodge, remove.
μετακινέω.sd: to stir to a place elsewhere, i.e. remove (figuratively)
μετακινέω.as:
μετα-κινέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: De 19:14 (סוּג hi.), Is 54:10 (מוּט), etc ;]
trans., to move away, remove (ὅρια, De 19:14). Mid., to remove oneself, remove, shift: metaph., ἀπὸ τ. ἐλπίδος, Col 1:23.†

μομφή.as:
* μομφή, ῆς, ἡ
(< μέμφομαι), poët. form of μέμψις,
blame, complaint: Col 3:13.†

μιμέομαι.as:
μιμέομαι, -οῦμαι
(< μῖμος, a mimic, an actor), [in LXX: Ps 30 (31):6, Wi 4:215:9, IV Mac 9:2313:9*;]
to imitate: II Th 3:7, 9, He 13:7, III Jo 11.†

μῦθος.long: an idle tale, fable, fanciful story.
μῦθος.der: perhaps from the same as G3453 (μυέω) (through the idea of tuition);
μῦθος.as:
** μῦθος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX: Wi 17:4 A, Si 20:19*;]
1.speech, conversation.
2.
(a)a story, narrative (Hom.);
(b) later, opp. to λόγος (a true narrative) = Lat. fabula, a myth, fable, fiction: I Ti 1:44:7, II Ti 4:4, Tit 1:14, II Pe 1:16.†
SYN.: λόγος, q.v.

ματαιολογία.as:
*† ματαιολογία, -ας, ἡ
(< ματαιολόγος),
idle or foolish talk: I Ti 1:6.†

μητρολῴας.long: a matricide, smiter of his mother.
μητρολῴας.der: from G3384 (μήτηρ) and the base of G257 (ἅλων);
μητρολῴας.as:
* μητρολῴας (Rec. -αλῴας, in cl., -αλοίας, v. Bl., § 3, 3; 6, 2), -ου, ὁ
(< μήτρρ + ἀλοιάω, to smite);
(a)a matricide: I Ti 1:9 (AV, R, txt., but v. infr.);
(b)a smiter of his mother: I Ti 1:9 (R, mg., cf. Ex 21:15, and v. Ellic., CGT, in l.).†

μετάλημψις.as:
* μετά-λημψις (Rec. -ληψις), -εως, ἡ
(< μεταλαμβάνω),
participation, taking, receiving: of food, I Ti 4:3.†

μονόομαι.as:
** μονόω, -ῶ
(< μόνος), [in Aq.: Ge 49:6;]
to leave alone, forsake: of a childless widow, pf. ptcp. pass., I Ti 5:5.†

μάμμη.as:
** μάμμη, -ης, ἡ
(onomatop.), [in LXX: IV Mac 16:9*;]
1. in cl., a child's name for mother.
2. In late Gk. (= cl., τήθη), a grandmother: (LXX, IV Mac 16:9), II Ti 1:5.†

μεμβράνα.long: a parchment leaf, perhaps for notes.

ματαιολόγος.sd: an idle (i.e. senseless or mischievous) talker, i.e. a wrangler

μεγαλωσύνη.as:
† μεγαλωσύνη, -ης, ἡ
(< μέγας), [in LXX chiefly for גְּדוּלָה and cogn. forms, II Ki 7:23, Ps 144 (145):3, al.;]
greatness, majesty: He 1:38:1, Ju 25 (elsewhere Eccl. only).†

μισθαποδοσία.long: (lit: repayment of price or payment of price due), reward, due punishment.
μισθαποδοσία.as:
*† μισθαποδοσία, -ας, ἡ
(< μισθός, ἀποδίδωμι; cl. μισθοδοσία),
payment of wages, recompense; meton.,
(a) of reward: He 10:3511:26;
(b) of punishment: He 2:2.†

μερισμός.long: (a) a distributing, a distribution, (b) a parting, dividing, severance, separation.
μερισμός.as:
μερισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< μερίζω), [in LXX for מַחֲלֹקֶת, מַחְלְקָה, Jos 11:23, Es 6:18*;]
1.a dividing, division: ψυχῆς κ. πνεύματος (i.e. between them or of the things themselves, v. Westc., in l.), He 4:12.
2.a distribution, bestowal (cf. μερίζω, 2); pl., He 2:4.†

μυελός.as:
μυελός, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX: Ge 45:18 (חֵלֶב), Jb 21:24 (מֹחַ) Jb 33:24*;]
marrow: He 4:12.†

μετριοπαθέω.g: I bear gently with, have compassion
μετριοπαθέω.long: I bear gently with, have compassion.
μετριοπαθέω.sd: to be moderate in passion, i.e. gentle (to treat indulgently)
μετριοπαθέω.der: from a compound of the base of G3357 (μετρίως) and G3806 (πάθος);
μετριοπαθέω.as:
*† μετριοπαθέω, -ῶ
(< μετριοπαθής, moderating one's passions),
to hold one's passions or emotions in restraint; hence, to bear gently with, feel gently towards: He 5:2.†

Μελχισέδεκ.long: Melchizedek, king and priest of Salem.
Μελχισέδεκ.as:
Μελχισεδέκ, indecl., ὁ (Heb. מַלְכִּי צֶדֶק),
Melchizedek: He 5:6, 106:207:1, 10, 11, 15, 17.†

μεσιτεύω.sd: to interpose (as arbiter), i.e (by implication) to ratify (as surety)
μεσιτεύω.as:
* μεσιτεύω
(< μεσίτης),
to interpose, mediate: ὅρκῳ, He 6:17 (MM, ii, iii).†

μετάθεσις.sd: transposition, i.e. transferral (to heaven), disestablishment (of a law)
μετάθεσις.as:
** μετά-θεσις, -εως, ἡ
(< μετατίθημι), [in LXX: II Mac 11:24*;]
1.change of position, removal: He 11:5.
2.change, as of that which has been established: He 7:1212:27.†

μισθαποδότης.as:
*† μισθ-απο-δότης, -ου, ὁ,
(v. supr.),
one who pays wages; meton., a rewarder: He 11:6.†

μηλωτή.as:
μηλωτή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< μῆλον, a sheep or goat), [in LXX for אַדֶּרֶת, III Ki 19:13, 19, IV Ki 2:8, 13, 14*;]
a sheepskin: He 11:37.†

μετέπειτα.as:
** μετ-έπειτα,
adv.
[in LXX: Jth 9:5, Es 3:13, III Mac 3:24*;]
afterwards: He 12:17.†

μαραίνομαι.long: pass: I die, wither (like the grass).
μαραίνομαι.sd: to extinguish (as fire), i.e. (figuratively and passively) to pass away
μαραίνομαι.as:
μαραίνω,
[in LXX: Jb 15:30 (יָבֵשׁ pi.), 24:24, Wi 2:819:21*;]
in cl.,
1. prop., to quench fire; pass., of fire, to die away, go out.
2. In various relations, to quench, waste, wear out (cf. Wi 19:21); pass., to waste away; in later writers (Plut., Luc., al.), of the withering of flowers and herbage (act., Jb 15:30; pass., Jb 24:24, Wi 2:8): Ja 1:11 (cf. ἀμάραντον).†

μετάγω.g: I turn about, change the position of
μετάγω.long: (usually: transfer, transport, and met: to a better mind), I turn about, change the position of; pass: I am brought back.
μετάγω.as:
μετ-άγω,
[in LXX: III Ki 8:47, 48, II Ch 6:37 (שׁבה) 36:3 (סוּר hi.), I Es 1:452:105:69, Es 8:17, Si prol. 1610:8, II Mac 1:33*;]
1. in Xen., Plut., and later writers, to transfer, transport (so LXX).
2. In sense otherwise unknown (v. Hort, in l.), to turn about, direct: Ja 3:3, 4.†

μετατρέπω.as:
μετα-τρέπω,
[in LXX: IV Mac 6:57:3, 1215:11, 18*;]
to turn about, turn (Hom., al., but not found in Att.) : c. acc., Ja 4:9 (WH, txt.; cf. μεταστρέφω).†

μώλωψ.long: a bruise, stripe, left on the body by scourging.
μώλωψ.sd: probably akin to the base of G3433 (μόλις)) and probably (the face; from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι)); a mole ("black eye") or blow-mark
μώλωψ.as:
μώλωψ, -ωπος, ὁ,
[in LXX for חַבּוּרָה, Ex 21:25, al.;]
a bruise, wound from a stripe: I Pe 2:24(LXX) (Arist., Plut., al.).†

μυωπάζω.long: I am short-sighted, blink, see dimly.
μυωπάζω.sd: from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι)); to shut the eyes, i.e. blink (see indistinctly)
μυωπάζω.der: from a compound of the base of G3466 (μυστήριον) and (the face;
μυωπάζω.as:
*† μυ-ωπάζω
(< μύωψ, closing the eyes, short-sighted; < μύω, ὤψ),
to be short-sighted: II Pe 1:9 (R, mg., closing his eyes; v. ICC, in l.).†

μνήμη.as:
μνήμη, -ης, ἡ
(< μνάομαι), [in LXX for זֵכֶר, זִכָּרוֹן;]
memory, remembrance, mention: μ. ποιεῖσθαι, c. gen., to remember, II Pe 1:15 (but in cl., π., μ. π. more freq. = to make mention, and so perh. here, cf. Mayor, in l.; and for ex. from π., v. Zorell, s.v.).†
SYN.: μνεία, q.v.

μεγαλοπρεπής.as:
μεγαλοπρεπής, ές (= μεγάλῳ πρέπων),
[in LXX: De 33:26 (גַּאֲוָה), II Mac 8:1515:13, III Mac 2:9*;]
befitting a great man, magnificent, majestic: II Pe 1:17 (cf. MM, xvi).†

μιασμός.as:
**† μιασμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< μιαίνω), [in LXX: Wi 14:26, I Mac 4:43*;]
1. prop., the act of defiling.
2. = μίασμα (q.v.): II Pe 2:10 (cf. Plut., Mor., 393c).†

μείζων.sd: larger (literally or figuratively, specially, in age)

μῶμος.sd: a flaw or blot, i.e. (figuratively) disgraceful person
μῶμος.as:
μῶμος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX, of physical blemishes: Le 21:17 ff., De 15:21, Ca 4:7, al. (מוּם); of mental defect, Si 20:24, al.;]
1. in cl. poets and late prose, blame, disgrace.
2. In LXX, perh. because of resemblance to מוּםpossible misspelling of מאוּם, a physical blemish (cf. ἄμωμος, I Pe 1:19, and v. Hort., in l.); metaph., of licentious persons, II Pe 2:13.†

μίασμα.as:
μίασμα, -τος, τό
(< μιαίνω), chiefly in trag. and late writers; [in LXX: Le 7:8 (18) (פִּגּוּל), Je 39 (32):34 (שִׁקּוּץ), Ez 33:31 (בֶּצַע), Jth 9:2, 413:16, I Mac 13:50*;]
a stain, defilement: pl., II Pe 2:20.†

Μιχαήλ.as:
Μιχαήλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. מִיכָאֵל, who like God?),
Michael, the Archangel (cf. Da 12:1): Ju 9, Re 12:7.†

μεμψίμοιρος.long: blaming one's lot or destiny, discontented, complaining.
μεμψίμοιρος.sd: akin to the base of G3313 (μέρος)); blaming fate, i.e. querulous (discontented)
μεμψίμοιρος.der: from a presumed derivative of G3201 (μέμφομαι) and (fate;
μεμψίμοιρος.as:
* μεμψίμοιρος, -ον
(< μέμφομαι, + μοῖρα, fate, lot),
complaining of one's fate, querulous: Ju 16.†

μέτωπον.as:
μέτωπον, -ου, τό
(μετά + ὤψ, an eye), [in LXX for מֶצַח;]
the forehead: Re 7:39:413:1614:1, 917:520:422:4.†

μεσουράνημα.long: mid-heaven, the middle of heaven, the zenith.
μεσουράνημα.der: from a presumed compound of G3319 (μέσος) and G3772 (οὐρανός);
μεσουράνημα.as:
*† μεσουράνημα, -τος, τό
(< μεσουρανέω, to be in mid-heaven, of the sun at the meridian),
the zenith, mid-heaven: Re 8:1314:619:17.†

μυκάομαι.der: from a presumed derivative of ( to "moo");
μυκάομαι.as:
** μυκάομαι, -ῶμαι, in cl. chiefly poët.,
[in Sm.: Jb 6:5*;]
prop., of oxen (onomatop.), to low, bellow; of a lion, to roar: Re 10:3.†

μασάομαι.der: from a primary (to handle or squeeze);
μασάομαι.as:
μασάομαι (Rec. μασσ-), -ῶμαι
(Aristoph. and late writers, but not in Trag. or in good Att. prose), [in LXX: Jb 30:4 (לֶחֶם), Si 19:9 A*;]
to bite, chew: Re 16:10.†

μάρμαρος.as:
** μάρμαρος, -ου, ὁ
(< μαρμαίρω, to glisten), [in LXX: Ep. Je 72*;]
1. any crystalline stone (Hom., Eur., al.).
2. In later writers, marble: Re 18:12.†

μύλινος.as:
*† μύλινος, -η, -ον
(< μύλος),
1.made of mill-stone (C.I. 3371).
2. = μυλικός: Re 18:21 (μύλον, T).†

μουσικός.long: skilled in music; subst: a musician, singer.
μουσικός.as:
μουσικός, -ή, -όν,
[in LXX: Ge 31:27, Ez 26:13 (שִׁיר), Da LXX TH 3:5 ff. (זְמָר), Si 22:6, al.;]
skilled in the arts, esp. in music; as subst., ὁ μ., a minstrel, musician: Re 18:22.†

μηρός.as:
μηρός, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for יָרֵךְ;]
the thigh: Re 19:16.†

Μαγώγ.long: (Hebrew), Magog, sometimes as name of a people, sometimes as name of a country in the Old Testament, probably the Scythians; hence: used in apocalyptic literature.
Μαγώγ.sd: Magog, a foreign nation, i.e. (figuratively) an Antichristian party
Μαγώγ.as:
Μαγώγ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. מָגוֹג, Ge 10:2, Ex 38:2, al.),
Magog, associated with Gog: Re 20:8 (v. Swete, in l.).†
